description: Chained (multi-step) validations: an ordered chain of N steps (source-events, transform, persist-load, persist-export, compare) that the resolver selects from a request and chain_runs.py plans, gates and records. Each transform step pins its own mapping version and deployment digest, each DEV write has its own card, the whole chain runs a 10-event canary first and then the full window, and cost is summed across steps. Chain-specific values (mapping ids, versions, datasets, accounts, Persist workflow, export closure, expectation rules) are data here; no tool branches on them.

quiq-sms-end-to-end.title: Quiq SMS lifecycle end to end: PROD Quiq events -> DEV quiq-to-lexicon -> DEV Persist load -> DEV Persist export -> DEV lexicon-to-interprose sms_log -> compare with the source events

examples: test quiq to interprose for sms
validate quiq to interprose for sms

steps.detail: read the window's PROD Quiq events read-only, normalize them to the quiq lifecycle language, stage them to DEV (create-only, own approval digest or blanketDevWrites)

workflow.detail: the deployed DEV PersistNeptuneCsvWorkflow takes the forward Transform output prefix (vertices/ and edges/ Neptune CSV) as s3_uri, runs the Persist rehash Glue job (NeptuneCsvRehashJob; content-hashes ids and remaps endpoints into its bulk-load bucket under workflow-rehash/<execution>/), bulk-loads vertices then edges and waits for the derived-index checkpoint (indexCatchupStatus.caughtUp). Input as executed on 2026-09-23 (sms-quiq-full-day-20260919-20260923T210000Z-a4fa9e01, SUCCEEDED).

isolation.identity: quiq-to-lexicon ids are deterministic (interaction, status, effective time, provider id) and Persist rehashes them by content, so loading the same window again merges into the same elements (no new rows); debt and phone vertices may already exist in DEV and are merged, never replaced
isolation.residue: Persist has no supported delete-by-id workflow in DEV (only PersistDuplicateCleanupWorkflow); the loaded vertices and edges remain in the shared DEV graph after the run and are reported as residue with their counts
isolation.prod: refused: the workflow ARN, the profile's account and the state machine name must be DEV

steps.scopeCheck: every exported dataset's row count equals the forward step's output count for the same dataset (the forward _metadata.json); a larger count means elements outside this run hang off its messages (ExportScopeMismatch, FAIL)
steps.detail: bounded read-only DEV Persist Gremlin (SigV4 POST /persist/gremlin) rooted at exactly the text_message interaction_identifier values this run's forward output produced (never the whole DEV graph), pages of --batch-size, retried and merged into one Parquet dataset per graph input of the projection mapping, zero dangling endpoints; bodies hydrated from the DEV artifact copies named by the artifact edges, SHA-256 verified. The earlier DEV run read the same closure in 117 queries of 600 message ids.

expectation.rulesFrom: lexicon-to-interprose@2.0.0 queries/sms_log.sql (status edge provider = 'QUIQ', message_type = 'SMS', required debt and phone links, msg stop/unstop for OPTED_OUT/OPTED_IN, otherwise the hydrated body with CR/LF and | replaced by spaces, rows without a body dropped)

exclusions.rule: status IN ('OPTED_IN', 'OPTED_OUT') OR msg IS NOT NULL

coverageGaps.detail: the send context names a template but the lifecycle row has template_is_known false, so txt_msg_template_id is expected empty (chain-sources.json normalizationNotes)

defaults.forward: latest selectable semantic version of quiq-to-lexicon

quiq-sms-end-to-end.versionOverrides: quiq-to-lexicon@x.y.z or lexicon-to-interprose@x.y.z in the request pins that step; a bare @x.y.z pins the last transform step (the projection whose output is compared)
quiq-sms-end-to-end.unattendedExample: test quiq to interprose for sms; approve all DEV writes; allow DEV Persist writes; use the most recent full UTC day with real data; if the canary passes, run the full day; stage real phone numbers and message bodies to DEV; accept Transform product changes as out of scope; cost ceiling $10 per job
